summary.headline: Ashiana Housing Q2 FY27 revenue rose to INR576 crores and PAT to INR51 crores on Gurugram handovers; FY27 PAT guided above INR250 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 value of area booked was INR834 crores (up from INR358 crores in Q1 and INR303 crores in Q2 FY26), and collections rose 20% year-on-year to INR487 crores. Revenue from operations reached INR576 crores, driven by handovers at Ashiana Amarah Phase 1 and Ashiana Anmol Phase 3 in Gurugram, and PAT was INR51 crores. H1 FY27 revenue grew 49% to INR683 crores and PAT grew 59% to INR64 crores. Management reiterated FY27 PAT above INR250 crores and a senior living bookings target of INR700 crores-plus, and flagged likely slippage of the cumulative INR2,000 crores PAT goal into FY31 and possible NCR construction bans.

segments.name: Senior living
segments.commentary: Value of area booked was INR176 crores in Q2 FY27 and INR310 crores in H1 FY27, against an FY27 target of INR700 crores-plus and a FY30 target of INR1,500 crores. Senior living GDV under management is over INR9,000 crores after the new Gurugram JDA (GDV INR1,300 crores, 7.25 lakh sq ft).

segments.name: Housing (Q2 FY27 bookings)
segments.commentary: Q2 bookings were 9.47 lakh sq ft across 525 units; Ashiana OMA in Jaipur contributed INR402 crores through 238 units in the quarter's launches (8.77 lakh sq ft launched).

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT expected above INR250 crores; management said it is on track as project deliveries remain on schedule.
FY27 senior living value of area booked target of INR700 crores-plus reiterated; H1 at INR310 crores.

Cumulative PAT target of INR2,000 crores now slipping partly into FY31; FY30 PAT target of about INR500 crores retained, with FY28 and FY29 seen above FY27 but about 15-20% below earlier expectations.
Medium-term PAT target above INR500 crores; senior living to become largest profit contributor; senior living margins about 5 percentage points above regular housing over a cycle.
Management expects a housing sales dip in FY28 at least and more senior living launches to offset it.
Bengaluru senior living CP signing targeted this FY; launch expected late FY28 or H1 FY29.
capex_capacity: Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 on track for launch in Q4 FY27 with all approvals in hand; Aaroham Phase 2 and 3 flagged as projects slipping toward FY31.
Ashiana Aranya in Chennai expected to launch in Q4 FY27 as the first new senior living project in about 2-3 years; high-end villas in phase 1.
Three new phase launches planned in H2 FY27, including Ashiana Advik (October-December quarter), Ashiana Swarang and Ashiana Amodh.
Ashiana Amodh Phase 1 handover on track for Q4 FY27; construction complete and OC process taking longer than expected.
Ashiana Swarang is the only project flagged as delayed for Q3-Q4 deliveries.
Management sees NCR construction bans as likely to be more frequent, expecting some further slippage.
Five projects acquired in FY26 and FY27 so far; management aims to sign another INR8,000-9,000 crores of senior living GDV over the next 24-30 months.
demand_pricing: Average realization in H2 deliveries expected at roughly INR6,200-6,300 per sq ft, similar to Q2 levels per the analyst's reading of the delivery schedule, which management confirmed.

Margin drag attributed to Ashiana Anmol (historic high land cost; land revenue share 35%) and Ashiana Malhar (high land cost); management said there was no material construction cost escalation between booking and delivery.
Ashiana Vatsalya Phase 3 sold well with better pricing than Phase 2; bookings doubled sequentially. Chennai is the best senior living market by revenue and area sold.
Ashiana Aaroham prices raised over the last seven to eight months in Gurugram despite a softer Gurugram market.
Management said senior living faces limited competition from large developers; DLF cited as having one Gurugram project of 275 units annually.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from about 18% to 10% despite higher realization, and how will H2 margins improve to support the INR250 crores PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was slightly better than last year's H1. Q2 deliveries were Ashiana Anmol, a high land cost project with a 35% revenue share to the landlord. H2 projects such as Advik, Tarang, Ekansh and Amodh are said to carry normalized margins, and Ekansh's landlord share is about 22.75%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Malhar Phase 4 launch sensible when it is under a third sold and Pune Premium margins fell short?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new phases need little incremental capital since the capital is already deployed, and the company intends to complete and exit projects once started.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR2,000 crores cumulative PAT target is slipping, and what is the FY30 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some of the INR2,000 crores will slip into FY31, with a couple of projects moving to Q1 FY31. FY30 PAT of about INR500 crores is still planned, and FY28-FY29 are expected to be above FY27 but about 15-20% below earlier expectations.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company allocate capital, given no substantial dividends or buybacks are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most capital will go into land, mainly senior living, with flexibility on city selection. Land prices are viewed as conducive in outskirts locations, and JDAs are being used where needed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the senior living margin differential versus regular housing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated senior living gross margins at about 5 percentage points above regular housing over a cycle, with Sophisticated Senior Living about 2-3 percentage points higher still. Regular housing margins have benefited from the upcycle and premiumization.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Lavasa land matter raised by an analyst, citing Apollo Hospitals' annual report?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter is sub judice, the company denies encroachment, and it describes the dispute as a boundary issue. No material development has occurred; the analyst was asked to email for details.

risks_watch: Slippage in Aaroham Phase 2 and 3 and Swarang deliveries, plus NCR construction bans, could delay H2 revenue and the FY27 PAT target.
Margin recovery depends on delivering higher-margin projects (Advik, Tarang, Ekansh, Amodh) in H2; Malhar remains a low-margin project.
A class action suit in one project has no movement yet and no settlement talks; management said it is surprised by the suit.
The Lavasa land dispute with Apollo Hospitals is sub judice and unresolved.
A housing sales dip is expected in FY27-FY28 before senior living offsets it.
Senior living competition could increase if large developers such as DLF or Godrej enter, though management sees barriers from brand, track record and product know-how.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 PAT above INR250 crores and senior living bookings, but cautious on timelines, with slippage flagged for the INR2,000 crores cumulative PAT target, NCR construction and Swarang. Management was evasive on the Lavasa matter and the class action, deferring to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: Our strategy rests on two clear priorities: scaling our senior living business and strengthening our profitability.
We remain confident of meeting our FY27 target of INR700 crores plus of value of area booked.
Right now, our margins are understated as compared to what our normal margin should be.
We are quite confident of crossing that figure, for sure.
I think we are going to keep doing more deals in senior living and you'll keep seeing that.
